purpose: Orphenadrine helps relieve pain and stiffness caused by muscle injuries, sprains, or strains. It is usually used along with rest and physical therapy to help your muscles relax. It can make it easier for you to move around and feel more comfortable during recovery.
how_it_works: Orphenadrine works on your brain and nervous system to help block the signals that cause your muscles to tighten up and spasm. It also has a mild pain-relieving effect. Think of it as helping your nervous system 'calm down' so your muscles can stop tensing and relax.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, blurry vision, dizziness, drowsiness, feeling lightheaded, constipation, difficulty urinating, fast heartbeat, and upset stomach. These are common and usually mild, but let your doctor know if they bother you.
warnings: Do not drive or use heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can make you drowsy or dizzy. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Do not take it if you have glaucoma, trouble urinating, myasthenia gravis, or a blockage in your stomach or intestines. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other muscle relaxants, sleep aids, or anxiety medicines, as they can increase drowsiness. Older adults should use this medicine with extra caution.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one 100 mg tablet taken twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and do not take more than prescribed.
